name: ZEPLIN-I
notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).
Boulby coordinate: the Atlas site record for the mine is a campus-grade point; the hall/cavern is not located by the papers read, so the facility's site record is referenced.
The collaboration attribution rests on the 2007 ZEPLIN-II paper's wording 'previous UK Dark Matter Collaboration experiments NaIAD and ZEPLIN I'.

The ZEPLIN-I result was disputed: Phys. Lett. B 637 (2006) 156 (astro-ph/0512120) argued the discrimination claim was not reliable; the ZEPLIN I team replied in Phys. Lett. B 642 (2006) 567 (astro-ph/0701859).

physics_goals.value: Search for WIMP nuclear recoils using the scintillation pulse shape in liquid xenon

summary.plain: ZEPLIN-I was the first of the ZEPLIN liquid xenon dark matter detectors, with about 3 kg of liquid xenon, run in the Boulby mine in north-east England in the early 2000s. It found no dark matter and set limits; the strength of its method was later disputed.
summary.technical: Single-phase liquid xenon scintillation detector with pulse-shape discrimination, 3.2 kg fiducial mass, 2800 m.w.e. at Boulby, with a liquid-scintillator Compton veto and lead shield. Three runs totalling 293 kg d fiducial exposure; spin-independent limit minimum 1.1e-6 pb. Predecessor of ZEPLIN-II and ZEPLIN-III.
